name: Nada Tunnel
facts: Built between 1910 and 1911 for the Dana Lumber Company, Nada Tunnel was originally 12 by 12 feet, but a stuck log load forced its height to be increased to 13 feet.
The tunnel earned its nickname, “Gateway to Red River Gorge,” after becoming a shortcut for motorists traveling along Kentucky Route 77 to the Daniel Boone National Forest.
After timber depletion, the railroad tracks were removed and a dirt road paved through the unlit tunnel, eventually evolving into the single‑lane road that carries traffic today.
